name: Dorsal approach to a proximal phalanx of the foot
aliases: dorsal midline approach to the toe phalanx
corridor: Dorsal midline interval over the toe through or beside the extensor tendon to the phalanx, keeping the digital neurovascular bundles on the sides protected

positioning.text: Position supine with the forefoot at the end of the table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Use the dorsal midline axis of the toe, since the digital arteries and nerves lie on the medial and lateral aspects.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal incision over the center of the toe from the MTP joint to the PIP joint.

superficial_interval.text: Either expose and retract the extensor tendon, or divide it with a Z-lengthening using short proximal and distal transverse cuts joined by a longitudinal midline cut.

deep_interval.text: Dissect the capsule on each side and insert small right-angle retractors to protect the neurovascular structures before capsulotomy or bone work.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with dorsal veins, extensor tendon, capsule, and the phalanx.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal digital nerves and the digital neurovascular bundles on each side and the extensor tendon are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The medial and lateral borders of the toe are the danger zones for the digital nerves and arteries.

retraction_hazards.text: Use small right-angle retractors on each side to protect the neurovascular bundles and preserve longitudinal dorsal veins.

exposure.text: Exposes the dorsal surface of the proximal phalanx from the MTP to the PIP joint.

limitations.text: Exposure is limited by the small size of the toe and the need to protect the side-lying digital neurovascular bundles.

indications.text: Indicated for fixation or osteotomy of a proximal phalanx of the foot.

closure.text: Repair the extensor tendon with a 3-0 suture if divided and close the wound with a running 4-0 self-absorbing suture.

complications.text: Complications include dorsal digital nerve injury, extensor tendon problems, and stiffness.

procedure_applications.condition: Dorsal open exposure of a phalanx is needed, for example for phalangeal fracture fixation or osteotomy

questions.question: Why is a dorsal midline incision chosen over the toe?
questions.answer: Because the digital arteries and nerves lie on the medial and lateral aspects, away from the midline.

questions.question: How is the extensor tendon managed in this approach?
questions.answer: It is either retracted or divided with a Z-lengthening for repair at closure.

questions.question: How are the digital neurovascular bundles protected?
questions.answer: With small right-angle retractors placed on each side before capsulotomy.
